primary.estimand: paired difference in uncapped excess SVI posterior-expected decision loss
primary.directionRequired: challenger mean excess loss below comparator and lower regret-weighted oracle-misranking bound
primary.superiority: one-sided 95% upper confidence bound below zero

prospectivePower.consequence: The bootstrap confidence classifications are reported but are not progression gates; the 120-business cohort is a directional and safety screen.

decisionRule: Proceed to the sealed audit only if cohort integrity, directional mean improvement, theorem misranking-bound improvement, P90 safety, P95 safety, both family safety checks, oracle-selection-rate safety, and immutable eligibility agreement all pass.

prospectiveAmendment.reason: A training-only power calculation showed that a mandatory 2% confidence-bound gate was severely underpowered at 120 businesses.
prospectiveAmendment.timing: Made before any validation outcome was evaluated; the previous draft was never executed.

governance: A superiority claim requires the one-sided 95% upper confidence bound to be below zero.
Passing validation means safe to proceed to adversarial audit, not statistically proven superiority.
Secondary endpoints cannot rescue a failed primary or safety gate.
A revision made after validation results requires a new method version and a new independent validation cohort.
The 80-business audit remains sealed until this frozen protocol permits progression.
